 NOV 10-12, 2026 // SF, CA 
 A YEAR OF AGENTIC CODING. ONE ROOM. 
 AIE CODE returns for its second annual code-focused summit. Catch up on the year with the world’s top agentic engineers, sharing the workflows and breakthroughs changing how software gets built. 
 800 admitted last year. 1.5 million talk views worldwide.
 A highly selective gathering. Invitations by application only.
 APPLY TO ATTEND 
 
 
 BECOME A SPONSOR 
 
 
 

 

 PRESENTED BY // SUPPORTED BY

 Wednesday, November 11
 Full livestream ↗ 
 Gimlet Labs
 November 11 · Main stage
 What will you build when AI is 10× faster? 
 Natalie Serrino Gimlet Labs Co-Founder 

 Natalie Serrino asks her agent to make a slide look better. It does. The result takes less time than she would have needed to redesign it herself, and she gets a slide she likes without becoming a designer.
 Read the talk → Watch at 0:11:26 ↗ 17 min 

 Anthropic
 November 11 · Main stage
 Rethinking Claude Code Best Practices 
 Lydia Hallie Anthropic Member of Technical Staff 

 A setup built around an older model can become an obstacle for a newer one.
 Read the talk → Watch at 0:00:00 ↗ 18 min 

 Cloudflare
 November 11 · Main stage
 cloudflare is a neolab 
 Michelle Chen Cloudflare Group Product Manager 

 Cloudflare built a distributed inference network around a bet: models would get smaller and faster, making the distance between the model and its user increasingly important.
 Read the talk → Watch at 0:40:09 ↗ 20 min 

 SpaceXSI
 November 11 · Main stage
 All Code Is Slop (Except Mine) 
 Lauren Tan SpaceXSI Principal Engineer 

 When an agent makes the same mistake again, it is tempting to add another warning to AGENTS.md. Lauren Tan wants the correction to land somewhere harder to ignore: the codebase, an API, or an executable check.
 Read the talk → Watch at 1:01:02 ↗ 18 min 

 Intrinsec AI
 November 11 · Online track
 Read the inference state before the agent acts 
 Speaker identity unverified Intrinsec AI 

 A guardrail can inspect a prompt before the model receives it and inspect a response after the model produces it. But between those checks, the model has already transformed its input into internal state. The talk asks whether an inference operator can use that state as an additional security signal.
 Read the talk → Watch at 1:30:40 ↗ 7 min 

 Harvey
 November 11 · Online track
 The harness has to finish the job 
 Joey Wang Harvey 

 Joey Wang opens with the scale of Harvey's internal agent platform: more than one agent starting every minute on average, around the clock, and thousands of agent-written pull requests.
 Read the talk → Watch at 1:37:50 ↗ 13 min 

 Amazon Web Services
 November 11 · Online track
 Specs have bugs too 
 Rajath Kotyal Amazon Web Services 

 An e-commerce specification says that an order should become a backorder when inventory is unavailable. Elsewhere, it says that no order should ever become a backorder.
 Read the talk → Watch at 1:50:46 ↗ 8 min 

 Meta
 November 11 · Online track
 From answering the page to sharing the on-call rotation 
 Chinmay Gandhi Meta 
 Swaapnika Motapothula Meta 
 Vlad Tsvang Meta 

 Twelve alerts arrive at two in the morning. An assistant can help explain a latency spike, inspect a deployment, and read a runbook. Someone still has to decide which alert matters, ask each question, connect the answers, and carry out the follow-up.
 Read the talk → Watch at 1:58:35 ↗ 16 min 

 Google DeepMind
 November 11 · Main stage · Excerpt
 I deleted 90% of my harness (And It Got Better) 
 Philipp Schmid Google DeepMind Member of the Technical Staff 

 An agent can reach the right answer while taking an unnecessarily expensive route. Philipp Schmid's harness experiments focus on that difference: two systems may look equivalent in an accuracy table, yet consume very different numbers of turns, tokens, and dollars to finish the same work.
 Read the talk → Watch at 2:21:16 ↗ 15 min 

 Databricks
 November 11 · Main stage
 The Rise of the Agent Workforce: Rethinking Agent Infrastructure 
 Ankit Mathur Databricks Member of Technical Staff 

 A broken data pipeline invites several plausible explanations. Perhaps an upstream job changed. Perhaps the data no longer matches an assumption. An agent can suggest each theory, but testing it against production may be the very thing an engineer cannot safely let it do.
 Read the talk → Watch at 2:46:35 ↗ 17 min 

 Sonar
 November 11 · Main stage
 Building a Safe Software Factory 
 Andrew Finch Sonar Staff Software Engineer 

 A coding agent makes it easier to produce a pull request. That does not settle whether the change should merge, whether it behaves correctly after deployment, or whether a vulnerability discovered next week changes the answer.
 Read the talk → Watch at 3:10:06 ↗ 14 min 

 Factory
 November 11 · Main stage
 Earning Autonomy: From Missions to Workstreams 
 Luke Alvoeiro Factory Member of Technical Staff 

 A team hands an agent a large goal, approves the plan, and returns later to completed work.
 Read the talk → Watch at 3:42:45 ↗ 15 min 

 Cline
 November 11 · Online track
 The Improvement Loop Is the Product 
 Ara Khan Cline 

 A coding agent can help build the system that makes coding agents better. That observation is easy to turn into a story about a distant intelligence explosion. Ara Khan instead begins with a nearer question: what should an engineer work on when a new model can erase the value of a side project overnight?
 Read the talk → Watch at 3:59:46 ↗ 27 min 

 Tanmay Sah
 November 11 · Online track
 An Agent's Change Is Not Safe Until Its Recovery Has Been Tested 
 Tanmay Sah 
 Dolly Sah 

 The coding agent has done what it was asked to do. It patched the repository, passed the tests, and produced a release. Then a downstream integration fails. Reverting the Git commit sounds like an obvious response, but the repository is only one part of the system the agent changed.
 Read the talk → Watch at 4:26:17 ↗ 17 min 

 Duolingo
 November 11 · Online track
 Duolingo's Test-Writing Agent Is a Pull-Request Lifecycle, Not a Prompt 
 Kush Agrawal Duolingo 

 Duolingo's iOS codebase contains roughly 1.8 million lines of code and a decade of accumulated decisions.
 Read the talk → Watch at 4:42:54 ↗ 13 min 

 Zenity
 November 11 · Online track
 A Skill's Instructions Are Not Its Behavior 
 Roey Ben Chaim Zenity 

 An agent reads cloud configuration, queries identity services, and probes instance metadata.
 Read the talk → Watch at 0:00:00 ↗ 15 min 

 TypeSafe AI
 November 11 · Main stage
 Beyond Better Assistants: Software That Can Make a Decision 
 Diogo Almeida TypeSafe AI Co-founder & CEO 

 A model can be impressive in a demo and still be unsuitable for unattended operation. Diogo Almeida makes that gap the center of his keynote. He likes the new tools; his objection is to treating a good assistant as if it were already a dependable automation component.
 Read the talk → Watch at 5:06:58 ↗ 23 min 

 Glean
 November 11 · Main stage
 Beyond Generation: Fast, Structured AI Decisions with Jev at Glean 
 Chinmay Goyal Glean Software Engineer 

 A search assistant makes many decisions that do not require it to write anything.
 Read the talk → Watch at 5:34:33 ↗ 16 min 

 UiPath
 November 11 · Main stage
 Your Automation Is Overthinking It 
 Chibi Vikram UiPath Engineer 
 Kevin Bernstein UiPath Principal AI Solution Architect 

 A workflow does not need to deliberate about every step.
 Read the talk → Watch at 5:52:15 ↗ 15 min 

 ZoomInfo
 November 11 · Main stage
 Your Judge Is Hallucinating Too 
 Brian Kennedy ZoomInfo Principal Engineer 

 An agent says it scheduled an email for Tuesday.
 Read the talk → Watch at 6:11:43 ↗ 11 min 

 Workday
 November 11 · Main stage
 Autocomplete for Actions: System One from the UI to the DB 
 Scott Roberts Workday 

 Workday users do not always arrive with an open-ended research problem. Sometimes they want their pay information, a time-off action, or a colleague's contact card. Scott Roberts asks what happens when an interface can recognize that intent quickly enough to prepare the action while the user is still typing.
 Read the talk → Watch at 6:24:42 ↗ 12 min 

 Microsoft
 November 11 · Online track
 Sub-Agents Are a Distributed System (And Nobody Gave You a Consistency Model) 
 Girish Konda Microsoft 

 An orchestrator delegates work to several agents.
 Read the talk → Watch at 6:37:54 ↗ 23 min 

 Nikolay Petrov
 November 11 · Online track
 Your SKILL.md is 70% of Things the Model Already Knows 
 Nikolay Petrov 

 A skill can teach an agent something it does not know, or it can steer the agent through a process it already understands.
 Read the talk → Watch at 7:00:53 ↗ 14 min 

 Lovable
 November 11 · Main stage
 What it takes to set intelligence free 
 Fabian Hedin Lovable CTO 

 Lovable nearly failed by building for agents too early. Fabian Hedin opens with that admission, not with the architecture diagram. In 2023, the team could see a future of agents delegating to agents, but the models available at the time could not reliably support the elaborate system they built around them.
 Read the talk → Watch at 7:26:06 ↗ 22 min 

 Ramp
 November 11 · Main stage
 How to build an agent that builds the culture 
 Zach Bruggeman Ramp Principal Software Engineer 

 Inspect began as Ramp's collaborative coding agent.
 Read the talk → Watch at 7:48:52 ↗ 15 min 

 Independent
 November 11 · Main stage
 Software Factories: Escape from Trash Mountain 
 Steve Yegge Independent Independent Advisor & Creator of Beads & Gas Town 

 Steve Yegge has spent the year trying to make agents run other agents.
 Read the talk → Watch at 8:06:23 ↗ 21 min 

 Independent
 November 11 · Main stage
 2026 in LLMs 
 Simon Willison Independent Creator of Datasette

findings.title: Post-event page still invites registration
findings.description: Page "AI Engineer Code Summit 2026: AI Engineering Conference, Nov 10-12, San Francisco" shows dates in the past (NOV 10-12, 2026) alongside active registration/apply language — a stale-content inconsistency.
findings.recommendation: Replace the apply/register CTA with a post-event path (recordings, next-year waitlist) or add a visible 'event has ended' notice.

findings.title: Dense link surface increases scan cost
findings.description: 238 distinct links compete for attention on "AI Engineer Code Summit 2026: AI Engineering Conference, Nov 10-12, San Francisco".
findings.recommendation: Group secondary links; keep the primary path visually dominant.

findings.title: Desktop: primary navigation has 11 items
findings.description: The top navigation exposes up to 11 visible items (more than 7), which makes the major sections harder to name at a glance.
findings.recommendation: Group navigation into 7 or fewer top-level sections; move the rest into sub-navigation or the footer.

findings.title: Desktop: missing site ID (trunk test fails)
findings.description: On 1 page(s) a visitor dropped in cold can't find: site ID. Persistent navigation should answer what site this is, what page they're on, the major sections, how to search and where they are.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing trunk-test signals (site ID) to the persistent header on every page.
